page.overview:
What is arithmancy?

Arithmancy was a magical discipline concerned with the numerical study and analysis of magic. It involved the study of the magical properties of numbers and the use of numerical calculations, charts and other mathematical methods to analyse magical phenomena and predict outcomes. Those who specialised in the discipline were known as Arithmancers.

Arithmancy had a wide range of theoretical and practical applications, serving many of the same functions in the wizarding world that mathematics did in the Muggle world. Although predicting the future through numbers and numerology was one application of Arithmancy,

Arithmancy also had more mundane mathematical applications. Knowledge of the discipline could be applied to financial figures, banking and transactions. Curse-Breakers were required to achieve a passing grade on their O.W.L. exam in Arithmancy, with banking and transactions forming part of their work. During an investigation involving Slug & Jiggers Apothecary in Diagon Alley, Cerberus Langarm confiscated the shop's accounts ledger, a lengthy book of financial figures, and delegated the task of examining it to Mathilda Grimblehawk and her partner. They in turn passed it to Sage Bragnam because he had studied Arithmancy.

Another major application of Arithmancy was prediction. Numbers and numerology could be used to predict future events, and learned methods of predicting the future using numbers.
